ideas.title: A2P Rejection Fixer for AI Receptionist Resellers
ideas.summary: For small agencies that set up AI phone receptionists (Retell, Vapi, Twilio direct) for locksmiths, trades and clinics: paste a 10DLC rejection, get a corrected campaign description, opt-in flow and sample messages for that exact case, plus a consent widget and log that run on the client's own site.

public.summary: Get your business texting approved by US carriers without paying for rejection after rejection.
public.problem: You set up an AI receptionist or text alerts for your business, and the carrier registration comes back rejected with a one-line reason like "invalid campaign description". You rewrite it, pay the review fee again, and wait another week. Nobody tells you what wording would pass.
public.forWhom: Small agencies and freelancers who set up phone and texting tools for local businesses, and the owners of those businesses.
benefits: Paste the rejection and get a corrected submission for that exact reason
Clear wording for unusual cases such as alerts sent only to the owner's own phone
A consent box and record that live on your own website
Fewer paid resubmissions and faster approval
A checklist of what your website must show before you submit

ideas.problemStatement: A2P 10DLC campaign registrations for small businesses come back rejected with terse codes ('invalid campaign description', 'multiple opt-in workflow description is incomplete or unclear', or no reason at all). Each resubmission can cost the $15 vetting fee and a week. Platform templates exist but owners and resellers keep failing, especially in edge cases: a sole-owner locksmith who only wants AI-receptionist job alerts on his own phone was rejected twice in a week (2026-11-02 and 2026-11-06), another reseller paid the $15 fee twice with no specific correction, and an HN commenter was rejected about three times for a company chatbot number.
ideas.description: The user pastes the rejection text or code and answers a short form about the business, who receives messages, how they opt in (web form, verbal on a call, owner-only) and which platform submits it. A rules engine keyed to the carrier and TCR rejection codes rewrites the campaign description, message-flow/opt-in description and sample messages for that case, and checks the client's live website for the items reviewers look for (SMS clause in the privacy policy, terms with frequency, rates, STOP and HELP, an unchecked consent box beside the phone field). For clients without a compliant opt-in, it generates an embeddable consent widget that runs on the client's own domain and records each consent (text version, time, source) so the opt-in description is true. An agency dashboard tracks each client's submissions, rejections and approvals. GoHighLevel users are out of scope because GHL now ships its own A2P widget and validation.
ideas.targetCustomer: Small agencies, freelancers and AI-receptionist resellers on Retell, Vapi or Twilio direct who register texting for local service businesses (locksmiths, trades, clinics, salons), and owner-operators who register themselves.
ideas.buyer: The agency or freelancer, from client-setup margin (they already charge or pay $50-$200 per registration), or the owner on a business card.
ideas.whyNow: Carriers tightened campaign vetting: Twilio made privacy-policy and terms URLs mandatory for campaigns from 2026-06-30 and introduced more specific shared rejection codes from 2026-09-15; AI phone receptionists are bringing many first-time small-business texters into registration, and Retell's forum shows a steady stream of rejections from June to November 2026.
ideas.founderFit: A rules engine plus form wizard and a small embeddable widget is a React/Flask/Supabase build Pisan can ship alone; the knowledge base of rejection codes and accepted wording is curated data work rather than a paid API. He teaches agentic-tool courses, so AI receptionist builders are a community he can reach, but he has no existing reseller network.

competitors.gap: Only for GoHighLevel sub-accounts; Retell, Vapi and Twilio-direct resellers get nothing from it.

competitors.gap: Scores a website before submission; does not rewrite a rejected submission or handle owner-only or verbal opt-in cases.

competitors.name: Hot Prospector A2P funnel generator
competitors.gap: Generates privacy, terms and consent pages; no rejection-code handling or per-client tracking.

competitors.name: Retell SMS campaign application docs
competitors.gap: Fill-in templates exist, yet users still get rejected and support replies case by case.

competitors.gap: An embeddable registration flow for platforms building on Twilio; not available to small resellers yet.

competitors.name: FastA2P
competitors.gap: A done-for-you service; slow and expensive for an agency doing many small clients.

keyFeatures: Paste a rejection, get a corrected submission for that code
Edge-case templates: owner-only alerts, verbal opt-in on AI calls, appointment reminders
Live website check against reviewer criteria
Embeddable consent widget and consent log on the client's domain
Agency dashboard of client submissions and outcomes

features: Rejection-code knowledge base for the 10 most common codes
Rewrite wizard producing description, message flow and samples
Website check for privacy clause, terms and consent box
Embeddable consent widget with a consent log
outOfScope: Submitting registrations through carrier or TCR APIs

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, Flask, Supabase (Postgres, auth), a small vanilla-JS consent widget; no paid API at runtime.

pricing.model: per-agency subscription with a per-fix option
pricing.pricePoint: $19 per fix pack, or $29/month for agencies with up to 15 clients
pricing.rationale: Free checkers cap what a one-off owner pays; agencies pay $97 per done-for-you registration today, so a self-serve fixer at a fraction of that is easy to justify.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 80 agencies x $29/month = $2,320 MRR, plus 40 one-off fixes a month x $19 = $760. Assumes the reseller count on Retell and Vapi forums keeps growing.
ideas.distribution: Answer rejection threads on community.retellai.com and the Vapi community with a free one-rejection fix, publish a public rejection-code guide, and list in AI-receptionist builder communities and Pisan's agentic-coding course network.

validationTest.method: A landing page plus a free hand-made fix for 10 rejected campaigns found in public Retell threads; track how many are approved on resubmission.
validationTest.successCriteria: 7 of 10 approved on the next submission and 3 agencies pay for a pack before the build.

ideas.moat: A growing dataset of rejection codes matched to wording that later passed, built from real outcomes, which platform templates do not have.
compliance: TCPA: the product prepares wording and records consent; it must say it is not legal advice.
Consent logs hold phone numbers and IP data: needs a data processing agreement and retention limits.
Accessibility: the consent widget must meet WCAG 2.2 AA (labelled, keyboard-usable checkbox).

risks.risk: Twilio or Retell ship their own guided fixer (Twilio's embeddable is in beta).
risks.mitigation: Stay multi-platform and focus on edge cases and agency workflow.

risks.risk: Carrier rules change often and break the rules engine.
risks.mitigation: Track Twilio's changelog and record outcomes to update wording.

risks.risk: Template wording alone may not fix rejections caused by brand mismatches.
risks.mitigation: Include brand-record checks and say clearly which rejections are not resubmittable.

scoreRationale.pain: Four independent rejection complaints from June to November 2026 (https://community.retellai.com/t/a2p-10dlc-campaign-rejected-owner-only-sms-opt-in/3787, https://community.retellai.com/t/sms-campaign-rejected-twice-for-invalid-campaign-description-with-no-specific-correction-details/3571, https://community.retellai.com/t/how-to-fix-this-sms-a2p-10dlc-campaign-application/3764, https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/items/50250948); not 5 because Retell's own templates exist and the reviewer found the pain is vague rejection reasons more than missing templates.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: Resellers pay $97 for done-for-you registration (https://fasta2p-portal.pages.dev/, https://help.smrtphone.io/get-help-setting-up-your-a2p-10dlc-registration-smrtphone-help-center) and the $15 fee per resubmission (https://community.retellai.com/t/sms-campaign-rejected-twice-for-invalid-campaign-description-with-no-specific-correction-details/3571), but free checkers (https://www.messagedesk.com/free-tools/sms-compliance-checker) cap a self-serve price.
scoreRationale.reachability: Public rejection threads on Retell's Discourse name the buyers directly (https://community.retellai.com/t/a2p-10dlc-campaign-rejected-owner-only-sms-opt-in/3787); no existing network.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Each part exists free somewhere (https://www.messagedesk.com/free-tools/sms-compliance-checker, https://hotprospector.com/a2p-compliance-guide/funnel-generator, https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/sms-campaign-application) and GoHighLevel bundles it for its own users (https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008307-pre-built-a2p-campaign-registration-with-chat-widget, https://gohighlevelassist.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007604-ai-powered-a2p-compliance-validation); the gap is the post-rejection fix for non-GHL resellers.
scoreRationale.feasibility: A wizard and widget are small, but Retell requires privacy and terms URLs on the client's own domain (https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/sms-campaign-application), so the widget must run there, and the knowledge base needs upkeep.
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Rules change often (Twilio's mandatory URL rule from 2026-06-30, https://www.twilio.com/en-us/changelog/a2p-10dlc-campaign-registration-will-require-privacy-policy-and-) and consent logs carry TCPA record-keeping exposure.

review.findings: Reviewer rescored 23 to 18. Pain 5 to 4 and willingnessToPay 4 to 3: free scanners and generators exist (https://www.messagedesk.com/free-tools/sms-compliance-checker, https://hotprospector.com/a2p-compliance-guide/funnel-generator) and Retell already publishes templates (https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/sms-campaign-application) yet users are still rejected. competitiveGap 3 to 2: GoHighLevel now ships a widget-first A2P flow and AI validation (https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008307-pre-built-a2p-campaign-registration-with-chat-widget). Feasibility 4 to 3: Retell needs privacy and terms on the client's own domain, so a page hosted on our domain could itself cause a rejection. complianceBurden 4 to 3: frequent rule changes (https://www.twilio.com/en-us/changelog/a2p-10dlc-campaign-registration-will-require-privacy-policy-and-) and consent-log liability. Twilio's Compliance Embeddable is in private beta (https://www.twilio.com/en-us/changelog/compliance-embeddable-USA2P10DLC-beta). Re-scoped from a pre-submission checker to a post-rejection fixer for Retell, Vapi and Twilio-direct resellers, with a widget on the client's domain, excluding GoHighLevel users. Four of five complaints are Retell threads, but the rejections come from carrier vetting, not a Retell bug.

gateGap.closedBy: The validationTest: if 7 of 10 hand-fixed public rejections are approved on resubmission and 3 agencies prepay, competitiveGap and willingnessToPay rise by a point each and feasibility is proven, which would bring the total to about 21-22 and promote it.

ideas.title: State Return Walkthrough for Micro Shopify Sellers
ideas.summary: For tiny US Shopify sellers losing Shopify's automated sales tax filing after 2026-12-31 and unwilling to pay $75 per return on a $20 tax bill: a field-by-field walkthrough of their own state's web return, filled from Shopify's free jurisdiction report, with due-date and zero-return reminders.

public.summary: File your own state sales tax return in minutes, with every box already worked out from your shop's sales.
public.problem: You sell a few hundred dollars a month and owe the state about twenty dollars in sales tax. The filing services charge around seventy-five dollars a return, and your shop's own filing service is ending. The state website asks for numbers in its own boxes, by county or district, and you are never sure which figure goes where, or that you must still file when you sold nothing.
public.forWhom: Small US online sellers, often one person, who are registered for sales tax in their home state or a few states.
benefits: Know exactly which number goes in each box of your state's return
Never miss a due date, including months with no sales
A saved record of every return you filed and how it was worked out
Keep filing costs to a few dollars a year instead of per return

ideas.problemStatement: Shopify Tax's automated filing files its last returns for sales through 2026-12-31 and has been closed to new stores; the replacements (BreezyFile, Kintsugi, Shopify's own) charge about $75 per return. A Florida seller was charged a flat $75 for a $19.94 Florida return and could not turn the service off. For a one- or two-state micro seller the state portal is free, but the work is translating Shopify's report into the state's own lines (Florida's discretionary surtax by county, New Jersey's ST-50/51) and remembering zero-sales returns.
ideas.description: The seller connects Shopify read-only (or uploads Shopify's free US Sales Tax report or a TaxEqual export) and picks their states. For each state the app shows the web return as the portal lays it out, line by line, with the figure to type in each box (gross sales, exempt and marketplace-facilitated sales, taxable sales, tax by county or district, collection allowance), and why. It schedules reminders by the state's assigned frequency, including zero-sales returns, and keeps a period-by-period record of the figures used. It does not calculate tax at checkout, file or remit. Launch with five states that have local-rate lines (Florida, New Jersey, Texas, Georgia, Ohio) and add states on demand.
ideas.targetCustomer: US Shopify sellers with low sales-tax liabilities (tens to a few hundred dollars per period), registered in their home state or two or three states, who were on Shopify's automated filing or never had a filing service.
ideas.buyer: The owner, on a personal or business card, from a very small software budget.
ideas.whyNow: Shopify automated filing ends with returns for sales through 2026-12-31 (most due January 2027) and is closed to new enrolment; vendors are actively marketing $30-$75 per filing replacements from October 2026.
ideas.founderFit: A per-state mapping table, a report importer and a reminder scheduler are careful data work Pisan can ship alone on Flask and Supabase; there is no paid API. He has no tax background, so the content needs checking against each state's published instructions, and his reach is the Shopify Community rather than a network.

keyFeatures: Line-by-line walkthrough of each state's web return
Import from Shopify or its free sales tax report
Due-date and zero-sales reminders on the state's schedule
Period record of figures used, kept for audits

features: CSV import of Shopify's US Sales Tax report
outOfScope: Filing or paying on the seller's behalf
mvpScope.buildEstimate: 3 weekends for two states, a weekend per added state

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, Flask, Supabase, Shopify Admin API (read-only orders) or CSV import; no paid API at runtime.

pricing.rationale: Must cost less than one $30 TaxCloud filing a year; TaxEqual's free one-state tier sets the ceiling.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 1,000 sellers x $24/year = $24,000 a year. Assumes a small share of former automated-filing users are micro sellers who self-file.
ideas.distribution: Answer Shopify Community threads about the end of automated filing in December and January, publish free state-by-state filing guides that link to the walkthrough, and list a companion app on the Shopify App Store.

validationTest.method: Publish a free Florida DR-15 walkthrough page for Shopify sellers before the January 2027 deadline and offer the tool for the second state; count sign-ups and paid pre-orders.
validationTest.successCriteria: 300 guide visits from Shopify sellers and 20 paid pre-orders at $24 by 2027-01-31.

ideas.moat: Maintained per-state line mappings, checked against each state's published instructions each period; tedious to keep current, which is the work sellers avoid.
compliance: Tax advice risk: present figures as a worksheet from the seller's own data, cite each state's instructions, and say it is not tax advice.
Data: read-only order data; no payment data stored.
Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA for the web app.

risks.risk: TaxEqual or Shopify adds per-state walkthroughs.
risks.mitigation: Start with states that have local-rate lines and keep the price below a single filing.

risks.risk: A wrong mapping leads to an underpaid return.
risks.mitigation: Show the source of every figure and link the state's line instructions.

risks.risk: Sellers with one simple state need nothing beyond the free report.
risks.mitigation: Target states with local or district lines.

scoreRationale.pain: One strong complaint (https://community.shopify.com/t/charged-75-for-automated-tax-filing-i-couldnt-find-how-to-cancel-on-a-19-94-tax-bill/707463), about a $75 fee on a $19.94 return that could not be cancelled; the New Jersey thread (https://community.shopify.com/t/do-i-really-need-a-new-jersey-tax-id-to-sell-on-shopify/669990) is a question, not a complaint.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: Merchants pay $75 a filing (https://apps.shopify.com/breezyfile), but a one-state micro seller can use the free report and the state portal, and TaxCloud charges $30 a filing to switchers (https://taxcloud.com/lp/trusted-shopify-filing-partner).
scoreRationale.reachability: Shopify Community threads on the filing change reach the buyer directly (https://community.shopify.com/t/charged-75-for-automated-tax-filing-i-couldnt-find-how-to-cancel-on-a-19-94-tax-bill/707463, https://community.shopify.com/t/shopify-tax-vs-avalara/686476); self-serve App Store listing.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: TaxEqual already gives filing-ready reports and reminders free for one state (https://apps.shopify.com/taxequal-sales-tax); only the field-by-field state walkthrough is uncovered.
scoreRationale.feasibility: Per-state mapping and upkeep is real work; Shopify's report already has the jurisdiction data (https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/enhanced-sales-tax-reports-now-available-for-monthly-filers).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Telling sellers what to type in each box is close to tax advice; TaxEqual explicitly avoids it (https://apps.shopify.com/taxequal-sales-tax).

review.findings: Reviewer rescored 21 to 15, close to a kill. TaxEqual (launched 2026-10-02) already reads Shopify orders, separates marketplace sales, produces filing-ready reports per state and sends reminders, free for one state (https://apps.shopify.com/taxequal-sales-tax). Shopify's free US Sales Tax report covers county and district figures (https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/enhanced-sales-tax-reports-now-available-for-monthly-filers), and community guides build county pivots (https://community.shopify.com/t/filing-sales-tax-getting-gross-sales-by-county-from-shopify-reports-a-brief-guide-instructions/302691). TaxCloud charges $30 a filing to switchers (https://taxcloud.com/lp/trusted-shopify-filing-partner). The Florida complaint is mainly about not being able to cancel, and the NJ thread is a question. Pain 4 to 3, willingnessToPay 4 to 2, competitiveGap 3 to 1, complianceBurden 4 to 3. Re-scoped from an order-sync product at $8/month to a cheap field-by-field walkthrough of state web returns plus zero-sales reminders, on top of the free report or TaxEqual exports.

gateGap.closedBy: The validationTest: 20 paid pre-orders at $24 before 2027-01-31 would show willingness to pay (to 3), and the January filing deadline should surface more merchant complaints (pain to 4); without both it stays a lead.

ideas.title: Consent Proof Log for Ghost Publishers
ideas.summary: For solo and small UK and EU publishers on Ghost: a small script and webhook that record, for every signup, the exact consent text shown, when, and where, and keep that record exportable after a member is deleted.

public.summary: Keep proof of exactly what each subscriber agreed to when they signed up to your newsletter.
public.problem: Your signup form shows one short consent line, and if a reader or a regulator asks what they agreed to and when, you have nothing but today's version of your site. When you change the wording, the old version is gone. When someone deletes their account, so is any trace of their consent.
public.forWhom: Independent writers and small publishers in the UK and EU who run their newsletter or membership site on Ghost.
benefits: A dated record of the wording each subscriber saw and agreed to
Answer a reader's data request in minutes
Records that survive wording changes and account deletions
No change to how readers sign up

ideas.problemStatement: Ghost's Portal signup allows one checkbox with about 115 characters of legal text, and a UK publisher says Ghost has ignored requests for better consent handling for eight-plus years. The reviewer found that multiple checkboxes are mostly not legally needed (a privacy policy is information, not consent) and that Ghost's theme forms already allow more; the remaining gap is proof: Ghost keeps no versioned record of which consent text a member saw, when, and from which form.
ideas.description: The publisher pastes a short script into Ghost's code injection and connects a member webhook. On each signup the script records the consent text and version shown, the form, page and timestamp, and a hashed IP; the webhook ties it to the new member. The log keeps each record after the member changes or deletes their account (with a retention limit the publisher sets) and exports one member's history as a PDF or CSV for a data access request. A text-version history shows when the wording changed.
ideas.targetCustomer: Solo writers and small media businesses in the UK and EU running paid or free newsletters on Ghost(Pro) or self-hosted Ghost.
ideas.buyer: The publisher, on a personal or business card.
ideas.whyNow: A June 2026 Ghost forum thread revived the consent request, and Ghost's 2023 signup-terms change still offers one checkbox with short text; UK and EU publishers keep asking how to prove consent.
ideas.founderFit: A small embeddable script, a webhook receiver and an export page are a weekend build on Flask and Supabase; there is no paid API. Pisan has no Ghost network; distribution is the Ghost forum and Ghost hosts.

problemEvidence.author: Shirley (weemediahq)
problemEvidence.summary: UK publisher: Portal allows one checkbox with a 115-character limit, too little for her legal text; Ghost has not fixed it in eight-plus years. A reply from a Ghost host disputes that three checkboxes are needed.

competitors.name: Ghost signup terms (Portal)
competitors.gap: One checkbox with short custom text; no record of which text a member saw.

competitors.name: Ghost custom members forms
competitors.gap: Allow several newsletter checkboxes and labels, but keep no versioned consent log.

competitors.name: Tally or Formspree plus Make
competitors.gap: Can store form submissions, but are not tied to Ghost members and need building per site.

keyFeatures: Records consent text version, time, form and hashed IP per signup
Keeps records after member deletion, with a retention limit
One-click export for a data access request
ideas.techStack: Vanilla JS snippet, Flask webhook receiver, Supabase; Ghost Admin API read-only; no paid API at runtime.

pricing.model: flat subscription per site, or one-off
pricing.rationale: The reviewer found no spend evidence and low perceived risk, so price must sit near zero.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 150 sites x $3/month = $450 MRR. A side product at best; assumes a Ghost host bundles it.
ideas.distribution: Post in the Ghost forum consent threads, offer it to Ghost hosts such as Magic Pages as an add-on, and publish a free guide to proving newsletter consent on Ghost.

validationTest.method: Ask in the Ghost forum thread and in two UK or EU Ghost publisher groups whether anyone has had a data access request or regulator question about consent, and offer a free beta.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 5 publishers report a real request or audit worry and 10 install the beta; otherwise drop it.

ideas.moat: Thin: a tidy integration and trust; a Ghost host bundle would be the main defence.
compliance: GDPR / UK GDPR: the service becomes a processor of consent records and hashed IPs; needs a DPA and retention controls.
It must not claim to make a site compliant.
Accessibility: the export page must meet WCAG 2.2 AA.

risks.mitigation: Keep it a one-weekend build and price it low.

risks.risk: Publishers see little risk and will not pay.
risks.mitigation: Validate with the forum test first and kill it if nobody has had a request.

scoreRationale.pain: One complainant in one 4-post thread (https://forum.ghost.org/t/gdpr-compliance-in-ghost-subscription-forms-we-need-your-voice/63118); a reply there says one checkbox is enough.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: No spend evidence; the complainant wants Ghost to fix it for free (https://forum.ghost.org/t/gdpr-compliance-in-ghost-subscription-forms-we-need-your-voice/63118).
scoreRationale.reachability: The Ghost forum reaches the buyer directly and Ghost hosts post there (https://forum.ghost.org/t/gdpr-compliance-in-ghost-subscription-forms-we-need-your-voice/63118).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Ghost's custom members forms already allow several checkboxes and labels (https://ghost.org/docs/themes/members/); only a versioned consent log is missing.
scoreRationale.feasibility: Small build, but tying script records to members needs webhooks and deletion handling (https://ghost.org/docs/themes/members/).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Storing consent records and hashed IPs for every customer makes the product a GDPR processor (https://ghost.org/changelog/signup-terms/ shows how little Ghost itself stores).

review.findings: Reviewer rescored 18 to 13, close to a kill. The original pitch (multiple checkboxes) misreads the law: a privacy policy is information under Article 13, not consent, and accepting terms is not GDPR consent; one checkbox is usually enough for a single newsletter. Ghost's own members forms (https://ghost.org/docs/themes/members/) already give several checkboxes, labels and magic-link double opt-in for free, and signup terms exist since 2023 (https://ghost.org/changelog/signup-terms/). Pain 3 to 2, willingnessToPay 2 to 1, competitiveGap 3 to 2, feasibility 4 to 3, complianceBurden 3 to 2. Re-scoped to a consent-proof log (text version, time, source, hashed IP, kept after deletion, exportable for data requests) at under $3/month or as a host add-on.

gateGap.closedBy: The forum validationTest: 5 publishers reporting a real data request or audit concern would add independent, recent complaints (pain and evidence count); a Ghost host agreeing to bundle or resell it would be the first spend signal. Without those it should be dropped.

runNotes.caveats: First run of 2026-11-09 (Monday, accessibility and regulatory compliance lens). Three provisional ideas ship (18, 15, 13); none cleared the gate of 22. Seven candidates were researched and adversarially reviewed: four killed (Tax Drift Watch, whose second complaint was from a Shopify staff account and which free Shopify Flow covers; One-Off Hold Guard and Flat-Fee Text Personalizer from the watchlist, both now served free; Packaging Declaration Ledger, already sold by four Shopify apps at $14-$29/month) and three rescored down (A2P 23 to 18, State Return Walkthrough 21 to 15, Ghost consent 18 to 13). The lens's biggest 2026 mandates (EU withdrawal button from 2026-06-19, EU legal guarantee notice and green-claims rules from 2026-09-27, PPWR) are real and widely complained about, but every one of them already has many paid and free apps on Shopify and WooCommerce, so they were rejected without review. Ideas 2 and 3 are weak leads labelled as such; idea 3 in particular should be dropped if its forum test finds nobody with a real data request. The watchlist is empty: both carried entries were reviewed and killed, and no unselected candidate reached 19. Constraint check: at most 2 per category (Accessibility & Compliance, Small Business Ops, Micro-SaaS: one each); all three have small-business buyers; one Weekend MVP and two Multi-week. Dates on vendor pages without a visible date (FastA2P, smrtphone) are the fetch date, 2026-11-09, and say so. Focus source C5 (Federal Register) yielded no usable mandate for this lens: its term search returned unrelated HHS, DOL and EPA rules, so the run's mandate evidence came from C10-style change events (Shopify ending automated filing, Twilio's campaign rules).
